text:
Baguette 

 Bon appétit. 

 
 Drive iOS simulators, real iPhones and Android emulators from one CLI and one browser page.
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

A single Swift CLI — baguette — plus a self-contained web UI that
drives your devices headless, without opening Xcode, Simulator.app or
Android Studio: one --udid , the same commands and page for every device,
and one that can't do something says so by name and exits 1.

- iOS simulators — everything below: boot them, stream their screens
 at 60 fps, dispatch taps, swipes, multi-finger and system gestures,
 keyboard and hardware buttons, read the accessibility tree, tail the
 unified log, take screenshots and recordings, and feed them a camera,
 a location, motion and a slower network — on iOS 26 and later, where
 the 5-argument HID call idb and AXe rely on stopped working.
- Real iPhones on a cable — touches, a live screen, screenshots,
 recordings, the pasteboard and the accessibility tree, through
 CoreDevice → real devices.
- Android emulators — boot and shut down an AVD, stream its screen,
 touches with two fingers, scrolls, buttons ( back too), keys and typing,
 through the emulator's own control API → Android.

 Demo

 

 

 

 Install

 

Apple Silicon with Xcode 26 — baguette links the private SimulatorKit /
CoreSimulator frameworks that ship with Xcode. If Homebrew complains about
Rosetta, see Troubleshooting.

- A real iPhone needs to be paired with Xcode, in Developer Mode, on the
 cable, unlocked, with its developer disk image mounted.
- Android emulators need the Android SDK's adb and emulator :
 $ANDROID HOME , $ANDROID SDK ROOT or Android Studio's
 /Library/Android/sdk .

 Run from source

 

The rest of development is in CONTRIBUTING.

 Quick start

 

Coordinates are device points (dp on Android), and --width / --height 
are the screen size in those points ( baguette chrome layout --udid 
tells you for a simulator). For a
long-lived session, pipe JSON gestures into baguette input — see the
wire protocol.

 Sponsors

Apps that use and support Baguette development:

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 AirBuild 
 
 
 Your idea. Your AI team. A working native iOS app. Build the app. AirBuild handles App Review. Specialized agents submit, respond, fix, and resubmit—automatically. 
 
 
 

 What it covers

Rows below are for simulators; other devices do the parts their pages list.

 Area What you can do 
 --- --- 
 Devices iOS simulators, real iPhones on a cable, Android emulators; all in one list and one page → real devices, Android, serve 
 Touches & gestures Tap, swipe, pinch, pan, streamed one- and two-finger touches, home-indicator and pull-down system gestures → touches, double-tap 
 Buttons & keyboard Home, lock, volume, action, Watch crown; keystrokes, typed text, paste and clipboard sync → buttons, keyboard, paste 
 Screen capture Screenshots, recordings, frame streams to stdout, one output-size vocabulary, 3D device renders → screenshot, stream, recording, capture-size, 3d-rendering 
 Accessibility The on-screen AX tree as JSON, hit-testing, a hover inspector in the browser → accessibility, ax-inspector, ax-hit-test-sweep 
 Logs Live unified log, filtered by level, predicate or bundle id → logs 
 Web UI Focus-mode page with bezel, a multi-device farm, a JS SDK for your own page → device-farm, chrome-bezel, baguette-sdk, serve routes 
 Device lifecycle Boot, shut down, repair input after Xcode 27's Device Hub → boot, device-hub 
 Device settings Orientation, appearance, contrast, text size, status bar, shake → orientation, interface, status-bar, shake 
 Simulated world Mac webcam or a file as the camera, GPS and routes, CoreMotion, network conditioning → camera, location, motion, network 
 Apps & files Deep links and URL schemes, drag-and-drop app install and Photos → deep-links, file-upload 
 Other screens CarPlay and paired Watch, iPhone Duo and its hinge, a cable-free iPhone mirrored over Wi-Fi (preview) → companion-screens, iphone-duo, hinge, device-twin 
 Plugins Add panels and commands from a trusted bakery; they run as subprocesses → plugins

install.title: Install
install.html:
brew install baguette

Apple Silicon with Xcode 26 — baguette links the private SimulatorKit / CoreSimulator frameworks that ship with Xcode. If Homebrew complains about Rosetta, see Troubleshooting.

  • A real iPhone needs to be paired with Xcode, in Developer Mode, on the cable, unlocked, with its developer disk image mounted.
  • Android emulators need the Android SDK's adb and emulator: $ANDROID_HOME, $ANDROID_SDK_ROOT or Android Studio's ~/Library/Android/sdk.
Run from source
git clone https://github.com/tddworks/baguette && cd baguette
swift run Baguette serve                # Swift 6.4; builds, then serves http://127.0.0.1:8421
swift run Baguette list                 # any command runs the same way

The rest of development is in CONTRIBUTING.
